question.prompt:
A sealed envelope contains a card with a single digit on it. Three of the following statements are true, and the other is false.

I. The digit is \(1.\)

II. The digit is not \(2.\)

III. The digit is \(3.\)

IV. The digit is not \(4.\)

Which one of the following must necessarily be correct?

solutions.explanation:
Statements I and III cannot both be true, because a single digit cannot equal both \(1\) and \(3\). Therefore at least one of these two statements is false.

Exactly one statement is false altogether, so II and IV must both be true, and exactly one of I and III is true. The digit must consequently be \(1\) or \(3\). Both possibilities work: when the digit is \(1\), only III is false; when it is \(3\), only I is false.

In either permitted case, II is true. Thus the statement that must necessarily be correct is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Use the single false statement
